article.headline: Thursday's verdict: [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again]] preaches, [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] keeps the hot seat warm
paras: The lights are off, the hot seat is not. Thursday night is in the books, and [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] goes to bed at the bottom of the race: 5.4 points on the board, a projected final of 96.6 and a Chop% of 36. Right above sits [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] at 7.7, projected for 98.1, Chop% 33. The seats were swapped late and nobody has moved since. Still 1.5 projected points to argue about until Sunday.

Up front it was a sermon. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] put up 52.9 before most of the league had laced a shoe. [[p:12481|Cam Skattebo (RB, NYG, #44)]] ran in two touchdowns and added 44 yards through the air for 28.7 points. [[p:8131|Isaiah Likely (TE, NYG, #9)]] caught nine balls for 127 yards and a score, 24.2 more. Chop%: zero. The congregation may be seated.

[[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] had the night's other good time. [[p:11566|Jayden Daniels (QB, WAS, #5)]] threw three touchdowns and two interceptions, a full evening's entertainment, and the horse that left the rail holds fourth with 23.8 banked and a Chop% of 4.

One scare for the medical tent. BerkIam's [[p:8136|Rachaad White (RB, WAS, #1)]] was injured during a play, then returned to the game, and it was [[p:8136|White]] who ground out the late points that lifted his team out of last. No status listed on him tonight.

Everyone else watched from the couch. [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]], [[t:MVeny|MVeny]], [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]], [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] have not scored a point, and none of them is sweating: the five carry a Chop% under 10 apiece, with SkyWalker still on the launch pad and Hockey Guy still looking for the rink.

Now the long wait. bmransom and BerkIam each park six starters until Sunday, and both have three going in the early games. bmransom needs that early crowd to come out swinging. If it does, the seats switch again. If it does not, the hottest chair in the league has found its owner, and the rest of Sunday is a countdown.

articles.headline: Breakfast football kicks off, and the bottom two can only watch from the stands
paras: The waiting is over, sort of. The week's first Sunday snap came in the morning game, and neither chair at the bottom has a player in it. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] still holds the lowest seat, projected 102.6 with a Chop% of 25. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] sits one up at a projected 104.7, Chop% of 20. The tape measure between them still reads about two points. Nobody has moved. Both are sweating in the bleachers.

The only turn came overnight, on paper. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] slid from second to sixth without scoring a point, projected 116.3, Chop% of 7, up nearly three. Projections giveth and projections taketh away. The Bengals and Falcons are carrying seven of our starters this morning, and every one belongs to a team already comfortable: [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] flies [[p:6770|Joe Burrow (QB, CIN, #9)]] and two Falcons, [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] sends out [[p:9509|Bijan Robinson (RB, ATL, #7)]], and [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]], already sitting on Thursday's 22.5, gets another turn. First quarter, nothing on the board yet.

The bottom gets its turn in the early window. outsiderightfoot puts five starters on the field at once; the Naber sends out three and keeps [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] for Sunday night. One big early game from either side and the two-point tape measure flips. Receipts still out.

articles.headline: Burrow and Chase feast at breakfast while the bottom two still can't get a plate
paras: The two-point tape measure between the bottom chairs hasn't twitched. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] still holds the lowest seat, projected 102.6, Chop% of 24, down a hair on paper and nothing else. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] sits one up at a projected 104.7, Chop% of 20. Neither has a player on the field yet. Both are still in the bleachers, watching other people eat.

And what a meal. [[p:7564|Ja'Marr Chase (WR, CIN, #1)]] has 7 catches for 130 yards and a touchdown before halftime, 22.6 points, and [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] now sits at 45.1 with a projected 144.5 and a Chop% of zero. [[p:6770|Joe Burrow (QB, CIN, #9)]] is 14 of 16 with a passing score and a rushing score, 17.2 points, and [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] has climbed from fifth to third. The casualty is on paper: [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] slid from second to sixth without taking a snap, Chop% up three to 8, while [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] bounced straight back to second. Projections giveth, round two.

Q2, 5:55 on the clock. The bottom finally gets its turn in the early window: outsiderightfoot sends out five starters at once, the Naber sends three and still holds [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] for Sunday night. Two points is one good catch. Receipts still out.

articles.headline: [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] rockets to second while the bottom four crowd one small table
paras: The tape measure still reads two points. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] holds the lowest seat at a projected 102.6, Chop% of 23, and [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] sits one up at 104.7, Chop% of 19. Neither has a player on the field yet. But the bleachers got crowded: [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] and [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] each watched their Chop% climb five to 19 without scoring a thing. Four teams, one small table, and only bmransom has a fork out, [[p:9224|Chase Brown (RB, CIN, #30)]] nibbling at 6.2 in London.

The turn belonged to [[p:9509|Bijan Robinson (RB, ATL, #7)]]: 80 yards and a touchdown on the ground, 50 more through the air, 24.5 points, and [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFreeSince03]] vaulted from fifth to second, Chop% down to 1. [[p:6801|Tee Higgins (WR, CIN, #5)]] caught a touchdown and [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] climbed back from sixth to fourth. Projections giveth, round three. The odd one out: [[p:6770|Joe Burrow (QB, CIN, #9)]] added a second passing score for 23.6, yet [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] drifted from third to sixth. The ship gained altitude and lost places.

Q3, 6:18 on the clock. Then the early window, where the receipts finally print: outsiderightfoot sends out five starters, the Naber three, MVeny six. One good catch is still two points. One quiet afternoon from the wrong team, and the table loses a chair.

articles.headline: London goes quiet; the bottom four still share one table and a two-point tab
paras: Final whistle in London, and the tape measure never moved. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] closes the session in the lowest seat, projected 102.6, Chop% of 23, without a player on the pitch. [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] had the only fork at the table: [[p:9224|Chase Brown (RB, CIN, #30)]] finished at 10.8, and bmransom still slid a chair to ninth. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] and [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] sit a hair above at 19 Chop% apiece. Two points still cover the lot.

Upstairs, the Bengals ran the show. [[p:6801|Tee Higgins (WR, CIN, #5)]] caught a second touchdown and [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] rose two more places to second, Chop% of 3. [[p:6770|Joe Burrow (QB, CIN, #9)]] threw a third score and ran one in for 29.6, yet [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] stayed parked in sixth with 44.2 already banked, the most of anyone outside the top seat. The ship keeps climbing and the tower keeps saying hold.

Next session is the early window, and the receipts print. outsiderightfoot is projected to be chopped and sends five starters out at once; the Naber sends three, MVeny six, bmransom two. One lively afternoon from the wrong team and the table changes shape. One quiet one from outsiderightfoot and the axe starts to whistle.

articles.headline: Receipts print: [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] pays up and leaves; [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] takes the empty chair at the bottom
paras: The early window is a quarter old and the two-point tab is torn up. [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] settled first: [[p:11632|Malik Nabers (WR, NYG, #1)]] took one catch 22 yards and bmransom climbed from ninth to seventh, Chop% down from 20 to 6. Into the empty chair drops [[t:MVeny|MVeny]], seventh an hour ago, ninth now at 25%. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] never left the lowest seat: five starters on the field, projected 87.4, Chop% up to 31.

The strange part is who moved MVeny. [[p:8136|Rachaad White (RB, WAS, #1)]] caught one ball for 45 yards, the hour's biggest move, and MVeny's 11.6 is the most anyone has added since the last chapter. MVeny slid two chairs anyway. That kind of morning. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]]'s policy turned up a clause: [[p:3294|Dak Prescott (QB, DAL, #4)]] put the ball on the ground and lost it. The Naber holds eighth at 23%.

Still to come: outsiderightfoot's five are mid-game, and [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] waits for Monday night, the biggest card left in the lowest hand. MVeny has six live plus a Sunday-night quarterback. Upstairs, the tower finally gave [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] clearance, up to fifth. For the next chapter to flip, outsiderightfoot needs one of those five to find the end zone before the bill comes due.

articles.headline: The bill arrives: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] past 50% while [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] and the Naber swap chairs
paras: Last chapter asked [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] for one touchdown from five starters. None arrived. [[p:8144|Chris Olave (WR, NO, #12)]] has four catches for 55 yards, which is honest work and not a rescue. The lowest seat is now projected 78.5, and Chop% has leapt from 31 to 55. That coin flip stopped being fair.

Above it, the two tenants swapped chairs again. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] added 22.9, the biggest haul of the hour, and climbed back to eighth at 12%: [[p:6786|CeeDee Lamb (WR, DAL, #88)]] has five catches, 85 yards and a touchdown. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] slid to ninth, yet its Chop% fell to 15, because the quarterback who dropped the ball last hour has thrown two scores since. The policy paid out and still cost a chair. Upstairs, the tower cleared [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] all the way to second: [[p:8151|Kenneth Walker III (RB, KC, #9)]] caught two touchdowns before halftime.

Still to come: outsiderightfoot's five are all mid-game, and [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] remains the Monday-night card nobody can play yet, projected 22.8. The Naber has three waiting for the late and night windows; MVeny has a Sunday-night quarterback. For the next chapter to flip, outsiderightfoot needs a second half that looks nothing like the first.

articles.headline: The touchdown came and the axe never moved: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] stuck at 56%
paras: Last chapter begged for one touchdown. [[p:13345|Jonah Coleman (RB, DEN, #20)]] finally punched one in, 16.1 and counting, and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] piled on 18.6 in the hour. The reward: Chop% crept from 55 to 56. The second half looked nothing like the first. The bottom seat looks exactly the same.

The chairs above kept squeaking. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] scored 15.0, but every neighbor scored too, so its Chop% jumped from 13 to 20. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] holds eighth with three starters yet to play. [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] bought the cheapest exit of the day: [[p:1466|Travis Kelce (TE, KC, #87)]] scored from a yard out and its Chop% fell to 1. Upstairs, [[p:8151|Kenneth Walker III (RB, KC, #9)]] sits at 36.8 with three touchdowns, and [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] holds second.

Still to come: outsiderightfoot's five live starters are all in the fourth quarter, and after them only [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] remains, Monday night, projected 22.8. MVeny has a Sunday-night quarterback; the Naber has a Sunday-night back and two late-window pieces. For the next chapter to flip, outsiderightfoot needs a fourth-quarter bounce before the early games go quiet. Once they do, that 56% coin lands Monday night or not at all.

articles.headline: The coin landed early: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] climbs out, [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] falls in
paras: Forget Monday night. The fourth-quarter bounce last chapter begged for arrived on schedule. [[p:12506|Harold Fannin Jr. (TE, CLE, #44)]] caught a touchdown, [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] piled up 21.1 in the hour, and its Chop% dropped from 56 to 13. Three chairs up, with a Monday-night quarterback still to come.

The empty chair now belongs to [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]]. [[p:3294|Dak Prescott (QB, DAL, #4)]] threw for 335 yards and two scores, then lost a fumble, and the Naber sits last at 39.5 with a Chop% of 40, up from 16. The policy has three claims left: two late-window starters just kicked off, and [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] waits for Sunday night, projected 21.4. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] scored 15.7 and still slid to 24%. Its quarterback also plays tonight.

[[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] joined the sweat. [[p:11564|Drake Maye (QB, NE, #10)]] opened 0 for 2 with an interception, minus 1.0 so far, and the Chop% climbed from 2 to 17 with four starters live. For the next chapter to flip, the Naber needs the late window to land before [[p:11584|Irving]] laces up. Otherwise Sunday night becomes a two-man coin toss: Irving for the Naber, [[t:MVeny|MVeny]]'s passer for the escape.

articles.headline: The policy paid out in full, and [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] is still last
paras: Sunday night's coin toss is in. [[p:11584|Bucky Irving (RB, TB, #7)]] paid the claim in full: two touchdowns, 28.5 points. It wasn't enough. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] finished at 77.2, still in the empty chair, and its Chop% leapt from 40 to 95. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]]'s passer threw four interceptions and still won the toss, done at 81.0.

[[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] skated off the ice. [[p:11564|Drake Maye (QB, NE, #10)]] shook off that early pick, threw three touchdowns (and two more picks for balance), and the team parked at 86.2, Chop% back to zero. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] banked 55.9 since the last chapter and is safe at 81.4.

One door is still open. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]], the team that climbed out last chapter, sits at 65.3, lowest on the board, with [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] just kicking off tonight, projected 22.8. Allen needs 11.9 to pass the Naber. Anything less, and the chair swaps owners again. The insurance company has never rooted so hard against Buffalo. Chop%: 95 for the Naber, 5 for outsiderightfoot.

articles.headline: Five-for-twelve and a pick: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] wobbles over the chair
paras: The insurance company got half its wish. [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] is 5-for-12 for 43 yards with an interception, just 1.9 points, and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] sits at 67.2, still lowest on the board. But the bettors in the booth aren't panicking yet: the Naber's Chop% slid from 95 to 70, and outsiderightfoot's crept up to 30.

Over in the Buffalo backfield, [[p:8138|James Cook III (RB, BUF, #4)]] has 18 yards on 12 carries for [[t:bmransom|bmransom]], who could nap through this and stay safe. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] has nothing left to file. The policy closed at 77.2. All it can do is stand by the phone and hope Allen keeps misplacing the ball.

It's Q2, 8:56. Allen needs 10.0 more points to lift outsiderightfoot past the Naber. We have him projected at 14.7, which would park the team at a projected 80.0, clear by 2.8. That's a cushion, not a fortress. One more pick, one stalled half, and the chair swaps owners right back. Chop%: 70 for the Naber, 30 for outsiderightfoot.

articles.headline: Allen finds the ball: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] climbs to the chair's edge
paras: Somebody answered the insurance company's prayer, just not the way it hoped. [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] stopped misplacing the ball and found the end zone, adding 7.1 points since our last call. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] climbed to 74.3, now just 2.9 behind. The booth's Chop% flipped hard: [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] jumped from 70 to 93, outsiderightfoot fell from 30 to 7.

The Naber's policy is still closed at 77.2. All it can do is watch the Buffalo game and hope for fine print. [[p:8138|James Cook III (RB, BUF, #4)]] keeps grinding for [[t:bmransom|bmransom]], 47 yards on 18 carries, safe as a bank vault.

It's Q3, 11:21. Allen sits at 9.0 and is projected for 18.1, which would carry outsiderightfoot to a projected 83.4, clear of the Naber by 6.2. Three more points and the chair officially changes hands. One more pick and a cold second half, and the Naber's phone might still ring.

articles.headline: Chair changes hands: [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] escapes, the Naber's policy lapses
paras: The booth asked for three more points. [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] delivered 5.9. [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] climbed to 80.2 and stepped over the body, now 3.0 clear. [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] sits frozen at 77.2, and its Chop% just ticked up 7 to a full 100. The fine print has been read, and nobody's coming.

The help came from the same Buffalo game. [[p:8138|James Cook III (RB, BUF, #4)]] has carried it 31 times for 107 yards and a score, piling 13.5 points onto [[t:bmransom|bmransom]], who was already safe enough to sleep through this. Allen kept his end of the deal too: 234 yards, a touchdown, and only the one pick.

Q4, 4:40. The Naber has no one left to play. Allen is projected to finish at 16.4, lifting outsiderightfoot to a projected 81.7. The only way the chair flips back is if Allen gives away more than 3.0 points before the final whistle. The Naber's agent is on hold, listening to the elevator music, praying for turnovers.

articles.headline: Claim denied: [[t:rushilk67|Like a Good Naber]] meets the axe as Monday's bell rings
paras: No turnovers came. The elevator music stopped, the hold line clicked, and the answer was no. [[p:4984|Josh Allen (QB, BUF, #17)]] closed out Monday night with 14.9 points, and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] crossed the line at 80.1, a full 2.9 clear of the chair. Every starter in the league has played. Week 9 is in the books.

Monday belonged to Buffalo. [[p:8138|James Cook III (RB, BUF, #4)]] carried it 31 times for 107 yards and a score, the day's best line at 18.7 points, all of it banked by [[t:bmransom|bmransom]], who finishes third at 115.8 and never once checked the rearview. Allen's 234 yards and a touchdown did the heavier lifting: they were the difference between outsiderightfoot sleeping tonight and packing a bag.

Up the track, [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] added 8.8 on the night to land at 95.6, and the ship took a scare along the way: a SkyWalker receiver was hurt during a play, then returned to the game. The week's flight log still belongs to [[p:8151|Kenneth Walker III (RB, KC, #9)]], whose 36.8 points topped every starter in the league. [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] somehow lost a tenth of a point on a Monday and still finished eighth at 81.0, just ahead of the line.

At the front, [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] finishes first at 127.9, with [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] second at 123.0. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] (81.4), [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] (83.1) and [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] (86.2) all sat out Monday and watched the scoreboard like it owed them money.

And so, a farewell. Like a Good Naber posted 77.2, held that number all Monday, and waited for an adjuster who never arrived. It was a policy with real coverage for eight weeks, and the fine print finally came due. The premiums are paid, the claim is closed, and the Naber walks to the chopping block with its head up. Like a good neighbor, it was there. Just not quite enough.
Next up: the week turns over Tuesday morning, and the Naber's roster hits the wire overnight into Wednesday. Nine teams remain, and the chair is empty again.

articles.headline: Week 10 opens with a garage sale and one team already smelling smoke
paras: The week turned over this morning, the scoreboard reads zeros across the board, and the chair is empty again. Nine teams remain. Like a Good Naber has walked to the block, and the wire is not a quiet place tonight.

Here is the thing about a garage sale: nobody has bought anything yet. The ten players the Naber dropped are sitting out on the lawn with price tags on. Waivers for that roster run overnight into Wednesday, and the league has made no moves since the chop. No claims, no FAAB bids, no trades. Everybody is standing at the edge of the lawn with their hands in their pockets, pretending not to look.

Which is fine, because the early line has a clear villain. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] is projected to finish last at 62.6 points, a long way back, and carries an 82% Chop%. The sheet already lists three of its starters as out, and that is a hole you cannot patch with good vibes. [[p:4034|Christian McCaffrey (RB, SF, #23)]] is projected for 23.7 and has to play like the whole offense. He does not have to do it alone, but he has to do most of it.

Behind the Christian, the gap is a canyon. [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] sits next at 8% and [[t:MVeny|MVeny]] at 6%, which is nervous territory but not panic. Then it flattens out: [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] a notch lower, and the rest of the field under 1%. [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]] sits second from the top at a projected 116.9, with only [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]] projected higher.

Nothing moves until the games do. Thursday night gets the first starters on the field, and Sunday opens the doors on everyone else. Until then, watch the wire: the Naber's leftovers go to somebody, and the team that needs them most is not hard to find.

articles.headline: Born again: [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] walks out of the fire, and [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] feels the heat
paras: Stop the presses. Tuesday's villain has left the building. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] opened the week at an 82% Chop% with three starters listed out. Tonight the sheet lists none, the projected finish has jumped to 118.1, and the Chop% is 8. Last place to fourth without a single point scored. I have called a lot of races. I have never seen a horse gain ground in the paddock.

Somebody has to smell the smoke, and the seat slid to [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]]: projected last at 104.0, with a 27% Chop%. [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] is next at 20%. Every score still reads zero, but Thursday night has kicked off, and both have a man on the field in the first quarter: [[p:8136|Rachaad White (RB, WAS, #1)]] for BerkIam, [[p:11632|Malik Nabers (WR, NYG, #1)]] for bmransom.

The Christian has two starters in this game as well, [[p:12481|Cam Skattebo (RB, NYG, #44)]] among them, so the great escape can get wider tonight. After [[p:8136|White]], BerkIam waits until Sunday for its other six. Only 3.3 projected points separate the bottom two. One big night from White, and the hot seat could change hands before the weekend.

articles.headline: [[t:MayebachMusic10|The Christian]] ascends, and [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]]'s hot seat starts to smoke
paras: The hot seat did not change hands. It got hotter. [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] asked for one big night from [[p:8136|Rachaad White (RB, WAS, #1)]] and has 1.1 points to show for it late in the second quarter. The Chop% has climbed from 27 to 34. [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] is no cooler: [[p:11632|Malik Nabers (WR, NYG, #1)]] has three catches for 8 yards, 2.3 points, and the Chop% is up to 25.

And the horse that gained ground in the paddock? He is running now. [[p:12481|Cam Skattebo (RB, NYG, #44)]] has a touchdown and 16.7 points, [[p:8131|Isaiah Likely (TE, NYG, #9)]] has added 6.9, and [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] owns the only real score on the board: 23.6. Fourth place to second. Chop% down from 8 to 1. Tuesday's villain is nearly out of sight.

Q2, 2:35, and a whole half still to come. The bottom two sit just 3.3 projected points apart, so [[p:8136|White]] and [[p:11632|Nabers]] are racing each other as much as the axe. After tonight, BerkIam waits until Sunday for its other six starters. One good half from White cools the seat. Anything less, and it smokes all weekend.

articles.headline: [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] bolts from the pack while [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]]'s seat goes from smoke to flame
paras: The good half never came. [[p:8136|Rachaad White (RB, WAS, #1)]] has 19 yards on seven carries and 2.9 points, and [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]]'s Chop% has climbed again, from 34 to 40. The race inside the race is slipping too: [[p:11632|Malik Nabers (WR, NYG, #1)]] lost a fumble and still crept to 5.9, so [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] now leads the bottom two by 4.8 projected points. It was 3.3 an hour ago.

But look up the track! [[p:11566|Jayden Daniels (QB, WAS, #5)]] has thrown two touchdowns, 16.2 points, and [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFreeSince03]] has gone from seventh to fourth in one quarter. Chop% from 15 to 5. Nobody saw that horse leave the rail. Up front, [[p:12481|Cam Skattebo (RB, NYG, #44)]] found the end zone a second time, 24.8 points, and [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] is a rumor to the rest of the field.

Q3, 4:06. [[p:8136|White]] has a quarter and change to cool a seat that is now on fire, and [[p:11632|Nabers]] has the same clock to pull away. When the whistle blows, both teams park six starters until Sunday. BerkIam needs White to win this last sprint, or it carries a projected 96.5 and the hottest seat in the league through the whole weekend.

articles.headline: Switch seats! [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] wins the last sprint and hands [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] the hot one
paras: He won the sprint! [[p:8136|Rachaad White (RB, WAS, #1)]] ground out a fourth quarter worth 4.8 points, up to 7.7, and [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] has climbed out of last. Chop% down from 40 to 33. The fire did not go out. It moved. [[p:11632|Malik Nabers (WR, NYG, #1)]] went backwards to 5.4, and [[t:bmransom|bmransom]], leading this little race an hour ago, now sits at the bottom with a Chop% of 36, up ten.

Up front it is no longer a rumor, it is a fact. [[p:8131|Isaiah Likely (TE, NYG, #9)]] caught nine balls for 127 yards and a touchdown, 24.2 points, and [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] has taken the lead with 52.9 on the board. [[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] holds fourth, the horse that left the rail still running.

Q4, 0:34. [[p:8136|White]] and [[p:11632|Nabers]] are all but done, and both teams park six starters until Sunday. Projected finals: BerkIam 98.2, bmransom 96.7. That is 1.5 points to argue about for three days. bmransom needs its Sunday early crowd to come out swinging, or the hottest seat in the league stays right where it just landed.

articles.headline: Thursday's verdict: [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again]] preaches, [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] keeps the hot seat warm
paras: The lights are off, the hot seat is not. Thursday night is in the books, and [[t:bmransom|bmransom]] goes to bed at the bottom of the race: 5.4 points on the board, a projected final of 96.6 and a Chop% of 36. Right above sits [[t:BerkIam|BerkIam]] at 7.7, projected for 98.1, Chop% 33. The seats were swapped late and nobody has moved since. Still 1.5 projected points to argue about until Sunday.

Up front it was a sermon. [[t:MayebachMusic10|Torn-Again Christian]] put up 52.9 before most of the league had laced a shoe. [[p:12481|Cam Skattebo (RB, NYG, #44)]] ran in two touchdowns and added 44 yards through the air for 28.7 points. [[p:8131|Isaiah Likely (TE, NYG, #9)]] caught nine balls for 127 yards and a score, 24.2 more. Chop%: zero. The congregation may be seated.

[[t:ZynFreeSince03|ZynFree]] had the night's other good time. [[p:11566|Jayden Daniels (QB, WAS, #5)]] threw three touchdowns and two interceptions, a full evening's entertainment, and the horse that left the rail holds fourth with 23.8 banked and a Chop% of 4.

One scare for the medical tent. BerkIam's [[p:8136|Rachaad White (RB, WAS, #1)]] was injured during a play, then returned to the game, and it was [[p:8136|White]] who ground out the late points that lifted his team out of last. No status listed on him tonight.

Everyone else watched from the couch. [[t:nomnomnomnomnom|nomnomnomnomnom]], [[t:MVeny|MVeny]], [[t:rafoster2124|Hockey Guy]], [[t:Dgt999|Kenny SkyWalker]] and [[t:outsiderightfoot|outsiderightfoot]] have not scored a point, and none of them is sweating: the five carry a Chop% under 10 apiece, with SkyWalker still on the launch pad and Hockey Guy still looking for the rink.

Now the long wait. bmransom and BerkIam each park six starters until Sunday, and both have three going in the early games. bmransom needs that early crowd to come out swinging. If it does, the seats switch again. If it does not, the hottest chair in the league has found its owner, and the rest of Sunday is a countdown.
